acceptedMechanicsParent: M047-I031 reducer ten-cylinder Bourdon pressure elongation
motivation: After accepted smooth-90 bend mechanics and reducer pressure ownership, L19 had only five source-end-action failures, all on ordinary straight source elements 4, 37, 38 and 44. I030 showed the source4/37/44 residuals persisted when replayed at CAESAR endpoint DOFs, so bend-network redistribution alone could not explain them. Locked ACCDB geometry ruled out a DELTA/coordinate mismatch on these spans. The remaining spans are unusually short relative to diameter (source4 L/D≈9.62, source37≈5.05, source44≈3.88), while the longer source38 L/D≈18.78 MZ row replayed below 10% at CAESAR DOFs. Re-test the previously qualified ordinary-FRAME transverse-compliance mechanism only after composing the now-accepted smooth-90 and reducer-pressure mechanics. This is an accuracy diagnostic, not a shear-led roadmap or production cutover.
heldMechanics: B31J smooth-90 bend correction 1.3/h from I029
bend arcs remain on the existing bend component formulation; no Timoshenko cutover on BEND_ARC
bend incoming straights remain unchanged; no Timoshenko cutover on BEND_INCOMING_STRAIGHT
B31J tee-modified FRAME carriers remain unchanged
reducer ten-cylinder stiffness/Schur condensation and I031 pressure free elongation

L20.interpretation: All compared L20 restraint components pass under this diagnostic composition, but the displacement/rotation failure count increases by four and 17 source-action rows remain above 10%; L20 is therefore not globally closed.

decisionReason: The exact-head real-ACCDB composition A/B strongly confirms that the remaining L19 error field is sensitive to ordinary non-tee straight-pipe transverse compliance after the independently accepted smooth-90 and reducer-pressure corrections are already present. The candidate reduces L19 restraint failures from 2 to 1, displacement/rotation failures from 57 to 33 and source-action failures from 5 to 1. Four of the five previously remaining source-action rows pass, node21470 FY passes at 2.83%, and the accepted reducer axial chain remains intact and improves. L20 restraint failures also fall to zero and source-action failures fall from 31 to 17. This is a mechanism result, not production authorization: the numerical 0.53 shear-correction input remains independently unverified as the exact CAESAR II metallic-pipe implementation, and tuning it to push node20090 FY (10.2208%) or source44 MZ (10.0561%) below the benchmark limit is prohibited. The next step must investigate those two residuals and/or independently establish the applicable straight-pipe transverse formulation without benchmark fitting.
acceptanceInterpretation: Retain the ordinary-FRAME transverse-compliance mechanism finding because it is population-wide, source-ID independent and consistent with the I030 fixed-DOF residual signature.
Do not promote kappa=0.53 or any nearby value to production merely because only two L19 rows remain slightly above 10%.
Do not sweep or fit a shear coefficient against BM4_NL targets.

I033 should first isolate node20090/source44 ownership among straight-span constitutive law, adjacent bend/load-case stiffening, Bourdon/load vector and recovery/interface mechanics while preserving I029/I031 custody.
L20 restraint closure is encouraging but does not waive displacement/source-action closure requirements.
